text:
maria: Heads-up — after the 1774200000 deploy I see a big drop in prefix-cache hit-rate for Private clusters. Noticed latency spike and token cost up ~2.1x for some customers.
kevin: ugh. numbers? which customers/regions?
maria: quick snapshot from last 30m: Hosted hit-rate 91.8% avg, Dedicated 87.6%, Private 45.9%.
kevin: thats... massive. any recent change to keying/normalization?
maria: yes — earlier today we landed normalizing prompt whitespace and lowercasing keys in runtime (PR #5123). It went to all environments.
olivia: @maria can you paste the profiling traces? I want to see whether the runtime is failing fast or just cold misses.
maria: pasted logs below:
```
[2026-03-17T10:04:12Z] cache.lookup prefix_key="user:123|prompt_hash:ab3f" -> MISS
[2026-03-17T10:04:12Z] cache.fetch backend=nfs path=/mnt/cache/prefix/ab3f latency=85ms -> OK
[2026-03-17T10:04:12Z] runtime.generate seq=1..256 kernel=matmul_v2 batch=1 latency=210ms
```
maria: On Hosted the backend is in-memory + SSD local, fetch latency ~1-5ms. On Dedicated similarly low. Private is hitting a central NFS (customer VPC), latency 70-120ms per miss.
ryan: So lowercasing + normalization changed keys enough to invalidate most existing cache entries in Private, causing a huge stampede to NFS.
kevin: Why did only Private get hit so hard? Shouldn't Dedicated have similar invalidation?
maria: Dedicated config had prewarm job enabled (prewarm-prefixes cron) that we run nightly. Private clusters had that disabled by default for security reasons. Also some Private customers had the old key namespace (case-sensitive) persisted on NFS with long TTLs.
olivia: Also batching heuristics amplify this — with cold KV misses we can't amortize kernel warmup. Batching drops to tiny sizes and kernel selection falls back to safe path, raising per-token cost.
kevin: Can we confirm regression is correlated with PR #5123?
maria: yes, bisected to the key-normalization commit. Reverting locally restores Private hit-rate to 89% in test cluster.
deploy-bot: deploy status: 1774200000 -> rollout complete to staged, hosted, dedicated, private (canary 10%).
laura: action items?
maria: immediate mitigations: 1) re-enable prewarm job for Private clusters by default (low risk). 2) hotfix: add a compatibility mapper that reads old key forms and writes normalized copies on first fetch (lazy-migration). 3) short-term rollback of PR #5123 if customers hit high costs.
ryan: +1 on lazy-migration — avoids global rollback and reduces NFS stampede. Need to be careful with metadata writes to NFS (rate limiting).
kevin: Do we have dashboards/alerts that should've caught this? Looks like cache-hit per-deployment metric is missing for Private.
laura: I'll add an alert: private.prefix_cache.hit_rate < 75% for 5m -> paging.
olivia: Also add a telemetry tag for "key-normalization-version" in future to make migrations observable.
maria: Performance note: when hit-rate >80% kernel selection picks fused_kv path; below that we often choose generic_attention kernel which is ~1.6x slower for our target seq lengths.
kevin: timeline? can we ship lazy-mapper today and re-run prewarm for Private?
maria: I can ship lazy-mapper PR in a few hours. Prewarm job toggle is config-only, rolling config will be trivial.
laura: I'll coordinate rollback if customers start to escalate. Ping me with PR link.
ryan: long-term: make prewarm optional but strongly recommended in setup docs for Private, and add an init-mode migration that runs once post-upgrade to rebuild prefix namespace into normalized keys.
olivia: Also we should add synthetic load test that simulates namespace migration to ensure NFS doesn't saturate.
kevin: Good plan. Also follow-up: check batching heuristics — can we detect flood of cache misses and temporarily increase batch sizes to better utilize kernels?
maria: interesting: currently we reduce batch size if observed latency > threshold; maybe inverse strategy during massive misses helps. Opened a ticket: PERF-887.
laura: thanks all. next steps: maria (lazy-mapper + PR), laura (alert + rollback plan), olivia (migration telemetry + synthetic test), ryan (init migration design).
maria: I'll post PR link when up. :raised_hands:
